contain.title: Uncropped variant (`fit="contain"`)
contain.description: Use `fit="contain"` when photos must never be cropped — the grid tile shows the full image at its natural aspect ratio instead of the default fixed-ratio crop.

grouped.title: Grouped tiles variant (`groupId`)
grouped.description: Set a shared `groupId` on two or more items to render them as one tile with an inline carousel and a count badge, instead of one tile per item — useful for a story/entry that has several photos. An item with no `groupId` still renders as its own single tile, shown alongside grouped tiles in the same grid.

standard.title: Standard
items: Use `SplitMediaGallerySection` when photos and videos must render in separate sections (default recommendation).
Use `MediaGallerySection` for mixed photo and video sections when a unified gallery is desired.
Keep media items in normalized arrays and pass them as props.
Keep `showFilters` optional and default to user-friendly category groups.
Core media visibility must not depend on JavaScript.
Use optional photo lightbox as enhancement only, not as primary access path; navigation (prev/next controls + keyboard arrows) is part of the standard behavior.
Optional page behaviors (shuffle, max photos/videos, info notice, social CTA, fit) are module props.
Empty-state copy is visible when no media items are provided (`items={"{[]}"}`).

Governance: gallery data lives in `src/data/gallery.ts`; caption text folds into `alt` fleet-wide (alt-only, no visible caption UI) even though `caption` remains a supported field on the type; galleries with more than ~9 photos should set `shuffleOnLoad` + `maxPhotos={9}`. Full contract: `gallery-module-wiring-contract.md`.

Optional `groupId` on `MediaGalleryItem` groups items into one tile with an inline carousel (via the shared `MediaCarouselTile` primitive) instead of one tile per item; give every item in a group the same `category`, since filtering stays per-item. The lightbox still cycles through every photo in the active filter, not just the group's.
